01.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, then Rabbi Hiyya
01.event: Yehoshua ben Levi visited Gavla, saw calf-sized grape clusters and cursed the land for feeding gentiles; the next year Hiyya visited and saw goat-sized clusters.
01.turn: The land shrank its produce in answer to the curse.
01.outcome: The locals told Hiyya to go away and not do to them what his colleague did.
01.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi came to Gavla and saw clusters of grapes as big as calves. He lamented that such fruit only fed the gentiles who ruled over Israel and told the earth to withhold it. The next year Rabbi Hiyya visited and saw clusters only as big as goats, and the locals told him to leave and not do to them what his colleague had done.

02.actor: A man who had never been married, and Rav Nahman
02.event: An unmarried man told Rav Nahman he had found an unobstructed orifice (non-virgin bride) on his wedding night.
02.turn: Rav Nahman doubted how he could know without prior experience.
02.outcome: Rav Nahman ordered him flogged with palm branches.
02.summary: A man who had never been married came before Rav Nahman and claimed that his bride was not a virgin. Rav Nahman reasoned that a bachelor could only know this through experience with prostitutes, and ordered him flogged with palm branches.

03.event: Rafram pressured Rav Ashi into giving a firm ruling in a case, and Rav Ashi collected the full value.
03.turn: Rav Ashi was pressured into an unequivocal ruling.
03.outcome: He collected the full debt value, treating the damage like a beam for a sculpture.
03.summary: There was a case like the one just discussed, and Rafram pressed Rav Ashi to rule firmly. Rav Ashi then had the claimant collect the full value of the document.
03.missing: The facts of the incident itself (who, what was forgiven) are not told; it only gestures at a case.

04.event: Funerals had become so costly that families abandoned the dead; Rabban Gamliel had himself taken out in plain linen.
04.turn: His self-deprecating example changed the custom.
04.outcome: Everyone followed, and today even rough cloth worth a zuz is used.
04.summary: Funeral costs had become so burdensome that relatives would leave the dead and flee. Rabban Gamliel set an example by being buried in plain linen, and all the people followed him. Rav Pappa notes that today people bury the dead even in cheap rough cloth.

05.actor: A dying man, Toviya, and Rabbi Yohanan
05.event: A man declared his property should go to Toviya and died; Toviya came to claim it.
05.turn: Possible doubt about which Toviya was meant.
05.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan ruled that this Toviya has come and takes it.
05.summary: A man told those present that his property should go to Toviya, then died. Toviya came to claim the estate, and Rabbi Yohanan said that Toviya had come, so there was no need to worry he meant someone else.

06.actor: Shmuel, his father, and Shmuel's daughters
06.event: Shmuel's father posted guards over captive women and Shmuel mocked it; later Shmuel's own daughters were captured and brought to Eretz Yisrael.
06.turn: The daughters, leaving their captors outside, claimed purity before Rabbi Hanina's court and were permitted to marry priests; the captors then came.
06.outcome: It was revealed they were Shmuel's daughters; their permitted status stood, and Rabbi Hanina told a priest to go marry one of them.
06.summary: Shmuel's father posted guards over captive women brought to Neharde'a, and Shmuel questioned this. His father asked whether he would be so dismissive if they were his daughters. Later Shmuel's daughters were captured, left their captors outside and told Rabbi Hanina's court each that she was pure, and were permitted. Their captors then came in, the truth emerged, and Rabbi Hanina urged a priest to marry one of them.

07.actor: Rav Pappa, Yehuda bar Mareimar, and Abba of Sura
07.event: Rav Pappa went to write his son's marriage contract with Abba of Sura; Yehuda bar Mareimar met him but balked at entering the house, fearing his presence would pressure the father to give a larger dowry.
07.turn: Rav Pappa pressed him to enter; his silent presence led Abba to write over everything he owned.
07.outcome: Yehuda said he did not want even that much; Abba offered to retract and Yehuda said he should uphold his word, though it was not to his liking.
07.summary: Rav Pappa went to Abba of Sura's house to arrange his son's marriage contract, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came to greet him but hesitated at the door. Rav Pappa pressed him in and he sat in silence. Abba thought he was angry and wrote all his property into the dowry. Yehuda said he did not want that, and Abba offered to retract, but Yehuda said he should not become a man who retracts his word.

08.event: Rava taught that one may scatter straw in a rain-damaged courtyard on Shabbat; Rav Pappa challenged him with a baraita.
08.turn: Rava realized his ruling was wrong.
08.outcome: He had a spokesman publicly announce his error and corrected the ruling.
08.summary: Rava taught that one may scatter straw in a rain-damaged courtyard on Shabbat. Rav Pappa objected from a baraita requiring a special manner. Rava then appointed a spokesman and publicly declared that his earlier statement was a mistake and gave the corrected rule.

09.event: The two disputed whether a person is liable on two counts or one in several cases, and each leaped up and swore by the Temple service that he had heard his view from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
09.turn: Contradictory oaths, so each argued logically.
09.outcome: Not resolved by narrative; later the Gemara speculates Bar Kappara mixed up cases.
09.summary: Rabbi Hiyya and Bar Kappara disagreed on whether a non-priest serving on Shabbat is liable twice or once. Each leaped up and swore by the Temple service that he had heard his answer from Rabbi. They then reasoned it through, and repeated the same dispute and oaths for two more cases.
09.missing: No real ending; most of the passage is legal analysis of why they differed.

11.actor: A man sent by his father to fetch chicks
11.event: A man climbed to a roof at his father's command, sent away the mother bird and took the young, and fell and died on the way back.
11.turn: He died despite fulfilling two mitzvot with promised long life.
11.outcome: Rabbi Yaakov took this as evidence reward is in the world to come.
11.summary: A father told his son to climb to the roof and fetch chicks. The son sent away the mother bird and took the young, fulfilling both honoring a parent and the mother bird mitzva, but on his return he fell and died.
11.missing: The passage shown [4]-[6] only argues about this incident; the story itself is in the preceding context segment.

13.actor: A man claiming another is a priest, and Rabbi Ami
13.event: A man came to Rabbi Ami saying another man had established presumptive status as a priest because he read first in the synagogue.
13.turn: Rabbi Ami questioned whether he read first as a priest or as a great man; the man answered a Levite read after him.
13.outcome: Rabbi Ami elevated the man to the priesthood on his word.
13.summary: A man came before Rabbi Ami and said that another man was a presumptive priest because he read first in the synagogue. Rabbi Ami asked whether that was due to priesthood or prominence, and the man replied that a Levite read after him. Rabbi Ami then elevated him to priesthood on that testimony.

14.actor: A man drinking wine and a woman who asked him for a cup
14.event: A woman asked a man in a shop for a cup of wine; he asked if she would be betrothed to him if he gave it.
14.turn: She answered only with a repeated demand to give her a drink, not agreeing.
14.outcome: Rav Hama ruled that such an answer is nothing and she is not betrothed.
14.summary: A man was drinking wine in a store when a woman asked him for a cup. He asked whether she would be betrothed to him if he gave it, and she answered only by repeating her request to be given a drink. Rav Hama ruled that this was meaningless and she was not betrothed.

15.event: Mar Yehuda found the residents of Mavrakhta placing their eruvin at the entrance of a synagogue and told them to place them farther in to gain more distance.
15.turn: Rava reacted dismissively, calling him argumentative and saying no one follows Rabbi Akiva on this.
15.outcome: Rava rejected Mar Yehuda's advice as following a discarded opinion.
15.summary: Mar Yehuda found people from Mavrakhta placing their eruvin in a synagogue and told them to put them farther in so more would be permitted to them. Rava called him argumentative and said nobody follows Rabbi Akiva's opinion on this, since the halakha follows the Rabbis.

16.actor: A man who rented a donkey, and the owner
16.event: The owner told the renter to avoid the Pekod River road where there was water; the renter took that road and the donkey died.
16.turn: The renter claimed there was no water and the death had another cause.
16.outcome: Rava accepted his claim on the principle of why would I lie, though Abaye objected that this does not apply where witnesses know there is water.
16.summary: A man rented out a donkey and warned the renter not to take the river road. The renter went that way and the donkey died. He came before Rava and admitted going that way but said there was no water, and Rava accepted his claim since he could have lied. Abaye objected that the principle fails when the facts are known.

17.actor: An Amorite and a resident of Eretz Yisrael
17.event: The Amorite asked how much the resident gathers from a palm tree on the Jordan bank.
17.turn: The Amorite jeered that Israel had already ruined the land since they got 120 kor.
17.outcome: The resident retorted he had only spoken of one side of the tree.
17.summary: An Amorite asked a resident of Eretz Yisrael how much fruit he took from a palm tree by the Jordan, and he said sixty kor. The Amorite scoffed that they got 120 and Israel had already ruined the land. The Israelite replied that he was speaking of only one side of the tree.

20.actor: A debtor, his creditor, and the purchaser of his land
20.event: A debtor owing 100 sold two plots for 50 each; the creditor repossessed one from a purchaser and then came to repossess the other.
20.turn: The second purchaser took 100 dinars to the creditor and offered a choice.
20.outcome: Not told in the passage; the creditor's response is not shown.
20.summary: A man owed a creditor 100 dinars and sold two plots of land for 50 each. The creditor repossessed one, then came for the other. The second purchaser took 100 dinars to him and said: if the plot is worth 100 to you fine, otherwise take the 100 and give up your claim on both plots.
20.missing: How the creditor responded; the ending is not narrated.
